html:
The first dynasty of China in traditional history, said to have ruled the middle Yellow River valley from about 2070 to 1600 BCE. The map shows it in 2000 BCE.

Later writers, above all Sima Qian, list seventeen Xia kings. The founder, Yu the Great, is said to have tamed the floods of the Yellow River by digging channels rather than building dams, and to have passed power to his son, starting rule by family. The last king, Jie, was a tyrant overthrown by Tang, founder of the Shang.

No writing from the Xia has been found, so whether it existed as told is debated. Many Chinese archaeologists identify it with the Erlitou culture, whose palace city near Luoyang flourished from about 1900 to 1500 BCE, with bronze vessels and large walled halls. Others think the Xia story was shaped much later, under the Zhou, to give the line of kings a worthy beginning.
sum: The first dynasty of China in traditional history, said to have ruled the middle Yellow River valley from about 2070 to 1600 BCE. The map shows it in 2000 BCE.
